"This agreement allows us to leverage the breadth and strength of Boeing to get our organization to the next level," said Steven Sliwa, president and CEO of Insitu. "At the same time, it allows us to retain the unique culture and environment that have driven the continuous innovation and entrepreneurial agility that have us positioned as a leader in our market." A unit of The Boeing Company, Boeing Integrated Defense Systems is one of the world's largest space and defense businesses specializing in innovative and capabilities-driven customer solutions.

Terms of the cash transaction were not disclosed. This transaction, anticipated to close by the end of September following regulatory approvals, does not affect Boeing's financial guidance. Once acquired, Insitu will be a separate subsidiary under Boeing Integrated Defense Systems' Military Aircraft unit.

Boeing and Insitu have partnered since 2002 and together developed the successful ScanEagle™ UAS program, which has more than 100,000 operational flight hours with the U.S. Department of Defense and international customers. results.title: Archer Aviation To Acquire Boeing's Wisk, SkyGrid And Insitu In All-Stock Deal
results.description: Archer Aviation and Boeing announced ... agreements for Archer to acquire three Boeing subsidiaries — Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu — in an all-stock transaction that will make Boeing one of Archer's largest shareholders and combine autonomous ...
extra_snippets: Archer Aviation and Boeing announced Monday that they have signed definitive agreements for Archer to acquire three Boeing subsidiaries — Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu — in an all-stock transaction that will make Boeing one of Archer's largest shareholders and combine autonomous flight, air-taxi and uncrewed defense technology under a single company.
Archer Aviation agreed to acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries, giving Boeing a stake of nearly 20% in the air taxi developer.

The deal marks a significant shift in the relationship between Archer and Wisk, which spent years as rival developers of autonomous air-taxi technology and were previously locked in litigation before settling their dispute in 2023 and entering a limited collaboration agreement that made Wisk an exclusive autonomy technology provider for Archer's aircraft. Monday's acquisition extends that earlier collaboration into full ownership. The transaction also continues a broader pattern of Boeing divesting businesses outside its core commercial aircraft, defense and services operations as the company narrows its strategic focus.

Combined, the three units bring roughly 2 million total flight hours to Archer's operations, along with entities including Insitu Pacific, Wisk Australia and Boeing Emirates. Archer plans to integrate the software architectures and flight histories of all three companies into ZEE, its proprietary artificial intelligence foundation platform for aerospace and defense, positioning the combined company as what Archer described as an "end-to-end physical AI platform" spanning commercial air taxis, defense systems and airspace management.
